paragraphs: West Yorkshire is a county area rather than a single council. Children in care here are looked after by five councils, Bradford, Calderdale, Kirklees, Leeds and Wakefield, each running its own fostering service, alongside the independent agencies shown above that work across the county. Each council area has its own page on this site: Fostering agencies in Bradford, Calderdale, Kirklees, Leeds and Wakefield.

Kirklees asks that carers are 21 or over, have a spare bedroom (or foster a child under three in their own room) and have time to give a child. Renting, being single, working or claiming benefits are not barriers. Its carers can foster short term, long term, as support carers for a day or a weekend, through short breaks for disabled children, or as supported lodgings hosts for young people of 16 and over, and they can join a Mockingbird hub of nearby foster families.

Our council pay pages show what two of the councils pay for 2026-27. Calderdale pays the government minimum by age plus a weekly skill-based payment of between £138.74 and £386.54. Wakefield pays an age-based allowance from £177 to £267 a week, a skill payment at one of four levels from £53 to £477, and up to £1,500 in welcome and loyalty payments in the first year.

Every fostering service in England must pay at least the national minimum allowance. Outside London and the South East, for 2026-27 that is £176 a week for a child aged 0 to 2, £182 for 3 to 4, £201 for 5 to 10, £227 for 11 to 15 and £267 for 16 to 17. Many services add a fee for the carer.
Wherever you live in West Yorkshire, speak to two or three of the services above and compare their training, support and pay before you decide.
